quarterly_data.signal: Interim CEO Pol Le Roux: FY2027 production will be 'fairly higher' than FY2026 (no number given); Mount Weld can deliver as much as Kalgoorlie and LAMP can process, and the constraints are concentrate quality and the last modifications at Kalgoorlie rather than demand. Lynas is working with Malaysian regulators to raise its concentrate cracking allowance to 110, which would add production in the quarter it is now limited; FY2027 capex covers the decided heavy rare earth separation investment plus stay-in-business and quick-win projects.

Interim CEO Pol Le Roux: the new heavy rare earth separation is on track, after dysprosium and terbium in 2025 and samarium a bit ahead of schedule in March 2026; gadolinium and yttrium are due in the first half of fiscal year 2028 and increased samarium and lutetium production in the first half of calendar year 2028. Lynas is the first DyTb supplier outside China, and the world outside China is very short of DyTb; terbium's commercial reception was more positive than expected.

Interim CEO Pol Le Roux: the Mount Weld expansion ramp-up is almost done except the TSF4 tailings facility; Kalgoorlie's MREC quality issues were fixed through a change in the precipitation process, its products and spares are now '100% non-China dependent', and minor gas-treatment modifications remain to reach nameplate. Kuantan had its best-ever cracking and leaching year (up to 31 tons a day at times) and has demonstrated 30 tons a day of NdPr finishing over several days, targeting 33; the roughly AUD 100 million industrial plant raised production by 50% and added DyTb. June-quarter ore variation at Mount Weld is now well under control, and Lynas is 'very happy' with the current quarter's production. LAMP could grow a lot beyond the 12,000 tons a year mentioned last year as a possible target, as demand justifies.
quarterly_data.figure: NdPr finishing 30 tons a day demonstrated, target 33 tons a day

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Gaudenz Sturzenegger: the AUD 34 million increase in G&A includes AUD 23 million of under-absorbed cost that will work itself out once Kalgoorlie fully ramps and about AUD 10 million, more than half linked to the leadership change, that is one-time; the cost base should ease, but the sulfuric acid price is four times what it was 12 months ago. Interim CEO Pol Le Roux: unit fixed costs should decrease over time.
quarterly_data.figure: sulfuric acid price four times higher than 12 months ago

quarterly_data.signal: Interim CEO Pol Le Roux: magnet demand from energy-efficient motors grows at about 10% a year, and car, wind-turbine and other OEMs are now serious about sourcing part of their supply outside China; many more offtake discussions with OEMs and new magnet makers are under way, including direct purchases by OEMs. Lynas is investing AUD 50 million in JS Link, which funds the rest of its Malaysian magnet project and whose IP was developed mostly with Japan; it partners with LS Cable on rare earth metal making and signed an MOU with Noveon Magnetics for US magnet making. Lynas offers magnet makers recycling of swarf (the 30% of raw material lost in magnet making) at its Malaysian facility, starting with JS Link, as a marginal investment; end-of-life magnet recycling will be substantial only after 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: AUD 50 million investment in JS Link

quarterly_data.signal: Interim CEO Pol Le Roux: Lynas will change the Mount Weld mining plan to reach the dysprosium-rich zones faster, which needs no new permit but adds anticipated mining cost to be disclosed soon; it is characterising the carbonatite and discussing ionic-clay resource deals. Its thorium extraction program has good pilot-scale results and an industrial pilot plant is being built, with the 2031 commitment 'challenging, but not impossible'.
